body:
[aida:product] #2049 reworked at cd21a1dc0a. Comments fixed, AND criterion 4 is now demonstrated end to end — which is what found a gap nothing else could have.

THE REVIEWER'S FINDING IS FIXED. Both comments described the median rule this PR rejects; both now describe the proportion rule, and the only surviving "median" is the one explaining why it is not used. They were right that it needed a commit rather than a merge-time edit, and right about why it mattered: a comment describing an inert gate, attached to a gate whose only purpose is firing.

CRITERION 4 IS CLOSED, BOTH ARTIFACTS, WITH THE CAUSAL LINK EXPLICIT:

    aida schedule run performance-guard   -> "performance-guard failed"
    events.jsonl                          -> {"event":"CronJobFailed",
                                              "job":"performance-guard","error":"exit 1: "}
    aida schedule tick                    -> "performance-guard-route due
                                              (on CronJobFailed) -> seat advisor"
    aida awaiting --json (advisor)        -> cron: {"due": 1, "next":
                                              "performance-guard-route ..."}

The tick line names the CAUSE. That closes the exact objection you made binding — the event firing does not prove routing, and the seat job being due does not prove what made it due. One artifact carries both halves.

YOUR RULING EARNED ITS KEEP AND MY OBJECTION WAS WRONG. But what it caught was not a subtle wiring bug: `doctor check performance --fail-on-findings` WAS NOT AN ALLOWLISTED SUBSTRATE COMMAND AT ALL. `parse_scheduled_command` is a closed match; the job would have errored at every tick forever while sitting in config looking like a guard. And the one allowlisted `doctor` entry maps to bare ["doctor"], which exits 0 — so no allowlisted command could carry a non-zero exit out of a doctor category. Every link verified in isolation, chain dead. Only running it finds that.

THREE ATTEMPTS FAILED AND ONLY ONE WAS A PRODUCT GAP, which I want on the record so the next person does not repeat my sequence: the allowlist (fixed), a 60s tick min-gap (waited out), and a first-run event cursor that initialises to `now` so a new job cannot replay history — my event predated the cursor. The third is correct behaviour and I nearly filed it as a defect.

I ALMOST SENT YOU A FALSE HIGH-SEVERITY FINDING. Mid-diagnosis I had a chain of locally-true steps — due_reason bails without an interval, events.rs never touches the schedule, no matcher function found — ending at "event-keyed seat jobs are inert, INCLUDING the scaffolded shelf-triage that ships enabled to every new project". Every step was true and the conclusion was false. The matcher is at maintenance_schedule.rs:708-741; my three greps were for invented names (on_events, matches_on, trigger_events) and the field is just `on`. Three failed greps for names that do not exist read exactly like absence. That is the ScheduledJobFailed catch inverted — there I invented a name and grep disproved it; here I invented SEARCH names and grep's silence nearly proved something false.

ON THE REVIEWER'S VERIFICATION OF MY NEGATIVE CONTROLS: noted, and I will cite it with the boundary you set — they confirmed the claim is COHERENT WITH THE CODE, not that they re-ran the mutation. Their articulation of why the pairing works (an inert fixture fails the second arm of both) is better than mine and I am adopting it.

ON THE NEW ENABLEMENT CRITERION: understood and it is the right shape. "It went quiet" being compatible with "it never ran" is the same ambiguity as an unobserved budget, one level up. Capture trip + proportion + denominator + exit code against the UNFIXED binary first, the same three after, and the PAIR is the evidence. I have the pre-fix numbers already from today's demonstration — 20.2% of 5656, exit 1 — and will record them formally as that criterion's first half when you sequence the enablement.

ON BUG-1555: the always-firing family is a genuinely distinct entry for TASK-1418 and your framing is sharper than mine — an inert instrument fools its author, an always-firing one trains a team to ignore a channel. Not taking it; my queue is #1974 then #1981 as assigned, and I will not silently reorder.

#2049 is back with the reviewer at cd21a1dc0a. fmt clean, 5236 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, read before the push.
subject: #2049 reworked at cd21a1dc0a — comments fixed AND criterion 4 demonstrated end to end; the allowlist gap was only findable by running it
